text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** NMC only makes sense in a few cases.

**Why LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. One guide compared a LiFePO4 station rated at 3,000 cycles to 80% capacity with an NMC one at 500 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). A database of 54 models found a median claim of 4,000 cycles for LFP versus 800 for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). With daily use, that's roughly 1.4 to 2 years for NMC versus 8 to 11 years for LFP.
- **Safety:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed. One test had an NMC cell peaking at 731 °C versus 259 °C for LFP ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP isn't fireproof, though. In one overcharge test it reached thermal runaway earlier, and the authors noted it was less hazardous once it got there ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). It's a real plus if the unit lives indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Price:** The premium has mostly disappeared. One retailer's data shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is much cheaper.
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. NMC survives mainly in older or compact units ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC has an edge**
- NMC cells store more energy per kilogram. But in finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. One database found only about 10% more Wh per pound for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some LFP stations are actually lighter per Wh than some NMC ones ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare the specific models you're considering.
- If you use it a few weekends a year or for rare outages, cycle count barely matters. Calendar aging will limit it first. An NMC unit could be fine if it's light and cheap.

**Things to watch for**
- **Cycle claims aren't uniform.** Check the end point, since "to 70%" promises less than "to 80%". Test conditions also vary by brand.
- **Cold weather:** Most stations of either chemistry won't charge below 32°F. Check the manual for your model. Some sources claim LFP is much better in the cold, but others found the limits depend more on the maker than the chemistry.
- **Check the spec sheet:** Some makers don't state the chemistry at all.
- **Already own a working NMC unit?** There's no need to replace it.
